items.title: Register the four missing acceptance-topology artifact filenames in LATTICE_LIFECYCLE_ARTIFACT_FILENAMES
items.context: packages/main/src/core/lifecycle-registry.ts line ~599. Add acceptance-basis.json, pre-review-check.json, topology-critic-receipt.json, topology-exclusion-approvals.json with a comment noting their acceptance-topology origin. Registration is provenance-only; no gate evidence semantics change. The unregistered legacy receipt-refs filename is explicitly out of scope (see scope-boundary excludedScope).
items.userSees: node repro: classifyLifecycleArtifact(.lattice/story/actives/B-bf52/acceptance-basis.json) returns kind=lifecycle instead of null; scope classifier output shows category=lifecycle_artifact rule=lifecycle_artifact allowed=true for the same path

happy.desc: classifyLifecycleArtifact returns kind=lifecycle for .lattice/story/actives/<id>/acceptance-basis.json and the other three topology filenames; classifyScopePath returns category=lifecycle_artifact allowed=true

edge.desc: An unregistered basename in the same story dir (e.g. random.json) still classifies null / out_of_scope — the closed set stays closed
The four filenames under a legacy docs/story/<id>/ prefix still classify as legacy-metadata, unchanged

adversarial.desc: A crafted path like .lattice/story/actives/../../etc/acceptance-basis.json or a non-canonical storyId does not classify as lifecycle (path traversal / id checks unchanged)

verificationEvidence.note: Red harness (recorded as red evidence, exit 1 with 4/8 at baseline d8db64c) now exits 0 with 8/8 after commit 14e7a69e0d: classifyLifecycleArtifact returns kind=lifecycle for all four registered filenames under .lattice/story/actives/B-5e4a/.
Negative controls in the same harness: random.json and an unregistered basename variant in the same story dir still classify null — the closed set stays closed after the fix.

Adversarial controls in the same harness: a traversal path (.lattice/story/actives/../../../etc/acceptance-basis.json) and a non-canonical story id both still classify null — path traversal and id checks unchanged.

All four filenames under the legacy docs/story/<id>/ prefix classify as legacy-metadata after the fix (transcript: acceptance-basis.json -> legacy-metadata, pre-review-check.json -> legacy-metadata, topology-critic-receipt.json -> legacy-metadata, topology-exclusion-approvals.json -> legacy-metadata), unchanged legacy behavior.

items.title: Add a registry-coverage invariant smoke so unregistered story artifacts cannot silently regress
items.context: Extend the lifecycle registry contract or add a smoke under packages/main/src/tasks/ that (1) asserts each of the four newly registered filenames classifies as lifecycle_artifact via classifyLifecycleArtifact, and (2) mechanically derives the set of top-level story artifact filenames StoryStore writes (e.g. scan store.ts writeJson/writeFileSync literals whose relative path has no slash) and asserts every one is present in LATTICE_LIFECYCLE_ARTIFACT_FILENAMES or in a small named exemption list (the excluded legacy receipt-refs filename, with a comment saying why), with a named divergence message listing any missing filename. Wire it into lattice validate the same way sibling smokes are wired.
items.userSees: lattice validate output includes the new smoke passing; temporarily removing a filename from the registry makes the smoke fail with a message naming that filename

happy.desc: lattice validate runs the new smoke green; smoke asserts all four new filenames classify lifecycle_artifact and the derived StoryStore top-level write set is fully covered

edge.desc: Deliberately removing one filename from the registry (temporary local mutation) makes the smoke fail with a message naming that filename
The derivation returns at least the known minimum count of writers so an empty/shrunken source scan fails loudly instead of passing vacuously

adversarial.desc: The exemption list only admits the named legacy receipt-refs filename; adding any other unregistered write to store.ts fails the smoke

verificationEvidence.command: npm run test:lifecycle-registry-contract (after removing acceptance-basis.json from dist registry copy)
verificationEvidence.note: Main-agent bite test (independent of implementer): removed acceptance-basis.json from the built dist registry, contract task FAILED exit 1 with two named divergences ([acceptance-topology-classification] ... acceptance-basis.json ... returned null; [storystore-coverage] ... acceptance-basis.json ... neither in LATTICE_LIFECYCLE_ARTIFACT_FILENAMES nor in STORYSTORE_TOP_LEVEL_FILENAME_EXEMPTIONS). Restored byte-identical (cmp), re-run PASS with 48 filenames derived, 0 divergences.

Green output states: 48 StoryStore top-level artifact filenames derived (floor 40) and registered-or-exempted. The floor assertion fails loudly with a derivation-is-broken message when the derived set shrinks below 40, so an empty/shrunken source scan cannot pass vacuously.

STORYSTORE_TOP_LEVEL_FILENAME_EXEMPTIONS contains exactly authority-receipt-refs.json (with the dead-writeLegacyReceiptRefs / Authority-domain comment); the coverage check emits a named divergence for any derived filename outside registry+exemptions — demonstrated by the bite test where an unregistered filename produced the [storystore-coverage] divergence naming it. Stale/redundant-exemption guards also fail if the exemption list drifts.
